- M13 (catalyst dimer inactivation) remains competitive, indicating inactivation pathways may be relevant.

- The aim is achieved by creating a condition where catalyst efficiency and product effects become rate-limiting, differentiating between dimer-dependent and monomeric mechanisms.
</reflection>

1. Test catalyst efficiency in dimerization-dependent mechanisms (M2/M3) by reducing available catalyst.
2. Activate product inhibition pathways in M12/M17/M15 through initial product.
3. Reveal inactivation differences between M13 (catalyst dimer inactivation) and M5/M2.
Low catalyst will penalize dimerization mechanisms (M2) more than monomeric ones (M5). Initial product will activate inhibition pathways in M12/M17 while testing reversibility in M1/M5.
